h.select_rule: Keep hypotheses whose mechanism is supported by a retrieved empirical finding or a widely replicated regularity, but whose conditional form is not commonly stated. Drop hypotheses that are obvious restatements of main effects. Keep diversity of fields and both directions.
h.strategy: Use the retrieved abstracts to identify interaction patterns that were actually measured (for example saturation of gains in strong configurations, redundancy among components serving the same role, or trainability trade-offs). Turn each into a conditional claim about when a one-field edit's effect is larger or smaller. Ground every hypothesis in measured evidence or a robust regularity rather than speculation. Prefer conditions that strongly shift overall parent quality or remove a substitute. Vary edited fields and conditions, and balance HIGHER and LOWER.

hyps.why: Another strong conv path into the output already exists, so an extra 3x3 conv shows saturating returns.
A parallel strong conv from the input already supplies features, so the gain from upgrading edge 0 is smaller.
With the direct path absent, removing edge 5 leaves fewer routes to the output and costs much more accuracy.
Deleting edge 3 hurts more when edge 5 is also missing, because the output then depends on fewer paths.
A skip shortcut matters more when an alternative route to the output is missing, because it restores a trainable gradient path.
With edge 0 absent, node 1 carries no signal, so a conv on edge 1->2 is almost useless.
Edge 4 reads from node 1, which is dead when edge 0 is none, so the conv adds nothing.
Node 1 carries rich conv features, so a conv on edge 2 can compose them into deeper representations.
A strong edge 0 gives node 1 useful features, so a conv on edge 4 exploits them.
Without edge 1, node 2 receives little signal, so a conv on edge 5 has less to process.
